summary: Restore the captured Matrix brightness, AUX brightness, and Vibe together after qualification so a runtime/persisted Vibe mismatch cannot prevent owner-setting recovery.

scoped_evidence.approved_architecture_reference: Existing f89 qualification transaction and HBNF /json/state settings API; no lifecycle or firmware change.
scoped_evidence.affected_subsystem: Host qualification settings cleanup. Firmware identity, release thresholds, candidate/recovery attempt counts, and live authority are unchanged.
scoped_evidence.root_cause: After the combined-feature check changed Vibe, the candidate runner required runtime and persisted Vibe to already match before any restore write. A mismatch therefore blocked restoring the captured owner baseline. The pinned f89 usermod accepts matrixBrightness, auxBrightness, and vibe in one HBNF state update and marks changed settings for persistence.
scoped_evidence.rollback_reference: Revert the qualification runner helper and focused tests. No firmware rebuild, candidate installation, recovery attempt, or lifecycle-state change is involved.
tests: python3 tests/test_r6_qualification_brightness_transaction.py: PASS; full owner settings restore repairs a valid runtime/persisted Vibe mismatch with one write and exact readback.
scoped_evidence.expected_efficiency_effect: Prevents a completed qualification cycle from stopping at settings cleanup solely because the test changed Vibe; one validated settings update restores all captured HBNF controls without another firmware build.
scoped_evidence.limits: Host tests do not prove a future device write or the 90-minute soak. f89 performance remains unqualified, and no live writes were performed.
